instruction: Add a slide note with the text "INFO" and change the background to green.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding note text 'INFO' and setting background to green (RGB: (0, 176, 80)). Evaluator checks both note text (50% score) and background color with tolerance of 20 (50% score). The note text is case-sensitive as indicated in the hint.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct note text, 0.5 for correct background color

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both instruction requirements: note text 'INFO' (case-sensitive) and green background color
Getter logic correctly extracts note text from slide.notes_slide.notes_text_frame and background RGB from slide.background.fill, handling both solid fills and master backgrounds
Metric comparison logic is appropriate: exact string match for note text (case-sensitive as per hint) and Euclidean distance with tolerance=20 for RGB color comparison
Expected values are semantically correct: note_text='INFO' matches instruction, bg_rgb=[0,176,80] is a valid green color
Postconfig properly saves file with Ctrl+S before verification, ensuring getter can access the modified state
Proper partial credit scoring: 50% for note text + 50% for background color
Edge cases handled: empty slides, missing files, None values return appropriate empty results
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter assumes first slide (prs.slides[0]). While this is reasonable for single-slide presentations, the instruction doesn't explicitly specify which slide. This is acceptable for typical use cases.

Minor: Background detection only handles fill types SOLID (1) and BACKGROUND (5). If user sets background using gradients or patterns, it may return None. However, instruction 'change background to green' typically implies solid color, so this is acceptable.
